name: EC2 Root Volume Replacement (Anti-Forensics)
description: The root volume is the disk the operating system boots from. An attacker who can replace it with an older snapshot can undo security patches, wipe forensic artifacts, and put a backdoored image in place. To operators it can look like a failed disk or a rollback. This is anti-forensics: the running server is still there, but the evidence on disk is gone. Root-volume swaps outside a documented recovery process are high signal.
mitigations: Rotate credentials if the actor is compromised
